newsitem.title: USA: Successories signs long term credit pact.
newsitem.headline: Successories signs long term credit pact.

text.p: Successories Inc, a specialty retailer of products for business and personal motivation, said Tuesday it has entered into a $16.5 million long term credit agreement with Provident Bank based in Cincinnati, Ohio.

The new financing agreement includes three separate tranches: a $7.5 million six year term loan, a $6.0 million revolving credit line and a $3.0 million seasonal working capital line. Both credit lines are committed for six years.
This agreement replaces an existing $8.5 million facility with American National Bank and also repays $1.25 million in subordinated debt, the company said in a statement.

"We are pleased to put this new financing in place as it gives us tremendous flexibility as we chart our future growth," said James Beltrame, president and chief executive officer. "The pricing and terms are very competitive and it is expected that this facility will meet most of our needs for the next several years."

Because a significant percentage of the company's revenues are generated during the holiday season, meeting seasonal working capital requirements has always been an issue. This new facility addresses this need with a seasonal working capital line and will ensure that Successories can meet all product demand for customers in all distribution channels year-round, the company said.
